title: Capture of Atahualpa at Cajamarca
summary: On 16 November 1532 in Cajamarca, Francisco Pizarro's Spanish force ambushed the Inca ruler Atahualpa when he entered the town square with an unarmed escort, killed many of his men and seized him. He was held for a gold-and-silver ransom and executed in 1533. Historians disagree on whether it was a battle or a betrayal.

uncertainty.note: Ancient Origins mentions accounts giving 15 November; EBSCO gives "May 16" (not used, conflicts with the other two sources).

where.historical_name: Cajamarca, a highland Inca city, in the Inca Empire

importance.justification: The seizure of the Sapa Inca gave Pizarro control over the Inca Empire; Ancient Origins says resistance lasted until Vilcabamba fell in 1572.

sources.title: Reading between the Lines at Cajamarca
sources.publisher: University of Texas at Austin, LLILAS Benson (Portal magazine)

sources.title: Pizarro Conquers the Incas in Peru (EBSCO Research Starters)

reviewer_note: Place is the town of Cajamarca; the sources name its square but give no separate coordinates, so the pin is the city point. Perspectives differ: UT Austin article (citing Covey) treats it as a betrayal rather than a battle. Casualty figures vary and are omitted.
